_comment_1: Hand-curated ticker renames for cases where brokers retroactively relabel old transactions after corporate actions.  Applied at PARSE time, before dedup — so the same physical event (same date/action/amount) showing up with different symbols in different CSV exports gets collapsed to one txn via the normal dedup pass.
_comment_2: Schema per entry: { from, to, before_date?, after_date?, note }.  before_date means 'apply the rename ONLY when txn date < before_date'; after_date = '... only when txn date >= after_date'.  Leave both off to apply unconditionally.  Both can be set together to apply only within a window.
_comment_3: Keyed by the `account` value the parser emits (e.g. 'Robinhood').  Not account_group — this runs before normalization.

Robinhood.note: Avidity Biosciences (originally ticker RNA) was renamed to RNAM mid-2025 when Novartis announced the acquisition.  Robinhood retroactively relabeled the post-rename stock-lending rows as RNAM in newer CSV exports but left them as RNA in older exports, which created duplicate SLIP rows after dedup.  A separate spun-off entity, Atrium Therapeutics, took over the RNA ticker on 2026-02-27 — those events MUST stay as RNA (different company).  Cutoff = the Atrium spinoff date.
